stewart_read: Customer volunteers a high bill figure and multiple months of high bills unprompted — a strong emotional anchor.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect this back — 'so even with panels you're paying $700, that's exactly why this design matters' — instead of letting it pass to the ownership question.

quote: he said he still had to pay some money for the solar panel when he bought the house
stewart_read: Customer reveals the system may still be financed (not fully owned), a detail directly relevant to whether Ion can help or must DQ — rep does not probe.
coaching_implication: Ask: 'Do you know if he's still making payments on it, or was that a one-time buyout?' — this is the schema's own vs. lease/PPA branch.

quote: I would definitely just check with him.
stewart_read: Rather than running the orphaned_flow question set live, rep punts the qualification entirely back to the customer to research on her own.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be avoiding wasting time on a system Ion likely can't touch. But schema requires asking the company name and working-status questions before ending pursuit — those take seconds and either DQ cleanly or route the lead.
coaching_implication: Run the two-question orphaned_flow gate (company name, is it working) before ending pursuit — costs 15 seconds, avoids losing a real lead.

quote: so what you recommend me to do?
stewart_read: Second explicit ask from the customer for direction — repeat instance of the same missed probe.
coaching_implication: This is the second chance to ask the qualifying questions; rep repeats the same generic redirect instead.

quote: I'll I'll take you off the list so we're not on the bottom of your calls.
stewart_read: Call ends with no appointment, no locked callback time, and the rep proactively removing the lead from further contact.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: if genuinely Ion-incompatible equipment, disengaging is correct. But the rep never confirmed that — the DQ basis is assumed, not verified.
coaching_implication: Before removing a lead from the call list, confirm the hard-DQ criteria (lease/PPA, different company, broken system) rather than assuming.

quote: I'm a call I'm a save the number, and I'll call you back when I have my husband answer.
stewart_read: Customer identifies husband as needed decision participant but no appointment or callback time is set — this is a soft, customer-controlled next step, not rep-owned.
coaching_implication: Rep should have offered to schedule a specific callback time with husband present rather than leaving it entirely to the customer to reach back out.
